item.title: Sacrifices pay off as Dhiksha Devi wins Tavua College Dux Award and secures Australian scholarship
item.description: Sacrificing holidays and family time to focus on her studies has paid off for 18-year-old Tavua College student Dhiksha Devi, who has been named the school's Dux of the Year. Devi was named the Dux after achieving 386 out of 400 marks in the 2025 Fiji Year 12 Final Examination.
item.content:encoded:
Sacrificing holidays and family time to focus on her studies has paid off for 18-year-old Tavua College student Dhiksha Devi, who has been named the school's Dux of the Year.

Devi was named the Dux after achieving 386 out of 400 marks in the 2025 Fiji Year 12 Final Examination.

Devi says receiving an award she has dreamt of for many years is a proud and emotional moment, especially knowing that her success is not the result of her efforts alone.

She says the support and blessings of her parents, teachers, friends and loved ones in Fiji and abroad have played an important role in her achievement.

Devi says she never expected to receive the award because Tavua College has many talented and hardworking students.

She says one of her biggest challenges throughout the year has been falling sick frequently due to stress, lack of sleep and sometimes forgetting to eat while concentrating on her studies.

She credits her parents as two of her biggest supporters, saying they ensure she has enough time to study without being burdened by household chores.

Devi encourages students who struggle academically not to lose hope when they fail or make mistakes, but to see these experiences as opportunities to learn and improve.

Insert: Failure is an opportunity to grow 17th Nov

Meanwhile, Devi has also been selected as a recipient of an Australia Awards scholarship to study Aviation Management at Griffith University in Queensland, Australia.

Devi hopes to return to Fiji after completing her studies to contribute to the country's development and inspire more girls to pursue a career in aviation.

SODELPA disciplinary committee to investigate Uludole and Komaisavai over Constitution Bill submissions

However, Uludole says he stands by what they said in their submissions which included the proposal that all land
item.content:encoded:
SODELPA Leader Aseri Radrodro says a disciplinary committee has been appointed to investigate party lawyer Jolame Uludole and Ratu Savenaca Komaisavai over concerns that they went against the party's directive when making their submissions on the Constitution Amendment Bill last Friday.

However, Uludole says he stands by what they said in their submissions which included the proposal that all land in Fiji should be owned by the iTaukei.

Speaking after the SODELPA Management Board meeting, Radrodro says the disciplinary committee has been appointed in accordance with the party's constitution and has been given a timeline to investigate the matter.

When asked whether Uludole has been suspended as the party's lawyer, Radrodro says they cannot pre-empt the committee's decision.

He says the Management Board has taken the necessary steps to ensure the disciplinary process is properly carried out in accordance with the party's constitution.

Radrodro says some party members and provisional candidates had raised concerns about being publicly vilified on social media, regarding issues raised during the submission to the Parliamentary Special Committee.

He confirms that two names have been referred to the disciplinary committee: Jolame Uludole and Ratu Savenaca Komaisavai.

When asked about concerns over the stability of SODELPA, Radrodro says the party has its ups and downs.

Insert: Radrodro on stability of SODELPA Nov 17

When asked whether SODELPA will still vote against the Constitution Amendment Bill, Radrodro says the party will restate the submissions made to Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka on 31st October during the public consultation, possibly tomorrow, depending on the time allocated to them.

In an interview with fijivillage News, Uludole says the party should read Article 7(j) of the SODELPA constitution.

When asked whether the party had agreed to their submissions, Uludole says he stands by what they said.

Uludole adds there are now disagreements over whether they were supposed to make their recommendations and then bring them back to the Management Board for endorsement.

item.title: FMA Town Hall Forum in Nadi at 7pm this Thursday
item.description: The Fijian Media Association Town Hall Forum will be held in Nadi from 7pm this Thursday. Members of the public are encouraged to come out and put their questions on the prolonged drought, the Constitution Amendment Bill and other key national issues.
item.content:encoded:
The Fijian Media Association Town Hall Forum will be held in Nadi from 7pm this Thursday.

Members of the public are encouraged to come out and put their questions on the prolonged drought, the Constitution Amendment Bill and other key national issues.

The panelists are Deputy Prime Minister Manoa Kamikamica, National Federation Party Leader Professor Biman Prasad, SODELPA Leader Aseri Radrodro, Opposition MP and People First representative Rinesh Sharma, NextGen Alliance Party Leader Apisai Moce, Liberation of Fiji Party Leader Veronica Malani, Kingdom Unite All People's Party's Ratu Manoa Sova and We Unite Fiji Party Leader Ruveni Nadalo.

The FMA Town Hall Forum will also be streamed live on all the media platforms.

Members of the public are invited to join the discussion from 7pm at the Fiji National University Namaka Campus in Nadi.

Whether your concern is the drought, Constitution Bill, the cost of living, jobs, education, health services or public accountability, bring the questions that matter to you.

You can also watch the live coverage on our facebook page, fijivillage at 7pm Thursday.
